title: Partnering with Preview: Lights, Inference, Action
gist: Sequoia is leading the seed round of Preview, an AI-native video creation and production platform founded by Stefan Fejes and Veljko Tornjanski that combines a timeline, infinite canvas and asset provenance tracking in one multiplayer workspace. The thesis: video models are now good enough to be 'the new camera,' but professional video tooling is still bolted onto legacy pipelines, and the workspace where creative decisions happen will capture the many billions of dollars of inference flowing through the category.

themes.theme: The AI-native tooling gap in professional video

insights.claim: Software development tooling has been rebuilt from scratch for AI over roughly two years, while video creation tooling has not, leaving its entire workflow organized around capturing, uploading, storing and editing large files.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Frames video production software as an unmodernized category ripe for an AI-native rebuild, analogous to the IDE-to-AI-coding transition.
insights.quote: Yet unlike coding, video creation remains stuck in the stone age, with its entire toolchain still built around capturing, uploading, storing, and editing enormous files.

insights.claim: Generative video models are now expressive enough to function as the new camera, shifting the binding constraint away from animation craft and $100M production budgets toward human creativity and token inference.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: If the bottleneck really has moved to inference and creativity, spend should migrate from production labor and VFX toward compute and creative tooling.
insights.quote: The bottleneck is no longer the technical art of animation or the $100M budgets for film crews and visual effects; it’s human creativity and token inference.
insights.locator: Generative video is at a threshold moment

insights.claim: Professional video teams currently run generation, review and production tracking in separate applications, workflows break down under the volume of generated material, and finished takes often cannot be traced back to their source for legal clearance.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Provenance and asset tracking, not generation quality, is named as the practical blocker to studio AI adoption — a specific wedge to underwrite in this category.

insights.claim: The absence of an AI-native tool suite for video is described as the single biggest roadblock to the film, TV and advertising industry adopting AI.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Positions tooling — rather than model capability — as the gating factor on industry-wide AI adoption timelines.

insights.claim: Preview is an AI-native video creation and production platform that merges a video timeline with an infinite ideation canvas in a single collaborative multiplayer workspace, lets teams generate with any model, and tracks every character, location and prop with a complete record of how each asset was made.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic generation plus asset lineage is the claimed product moat; watch whether provenance becomes table stakes or a defensible layer.
insights.quote: Teams can generate with any model and track every character, location, and prop, with complete records of how every asset was made.

insights.claim: More than 100 studios are already actively using Preview, spanning agencies producing commercials for Fortune 500 brands, AI-native studios, and Hollywood feature filmmakers.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A concrete pre-seed-stage traction datapoint showing adoption reaches both incumbent Hollywood and AI-native production shops.

insights.claim: Preview's co-founders Stefan Fejes and Veljko Tornjanski were founding team members at video creation company Veed, and later at Vizcom where Veljko was the first hire and Head of AI while Stefan led Product.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Founder-market fit rests on prior operating roles at two earlier creative-tool companies rather than on studio-side experience.

themes.theme: Where value accrues in the video inference stack

insights.claim: Many billions of dollars of inference are expected to run through the professional video creation category, and value will accrue not to the models but to the platform where creative decisions get made and the record gets kept.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: An explicit bet that the workflow/system-of-record layer, not the model layer, captures margin in generative video — the key debate to test in this stack.
insights.quote: Value will accrue to where the work actually happens—the platform a creative team opens in the morning and closes at night, where the decisions get made and the record gets kept.
